name: Extended Existential with a Predicate
pattern: Clause[dummy there + be + pivot NP + integrated location or secondary predication]

entry.name: Extended Existential with a Predicate
entry.pattern: Clause[dummy there + be + pivot NP + integrated location or secondary predication]

1.definition: Introduces a referent and characterizes its position or current situation.

projection.target: Ringing predicates an activity of the alarms. A free event adjunct can instead modify the whole existential assertion without predicating a property of the pivot.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: There were two alarms ringing
curious.summary: A there sentence can introduce something and then say where it is or what it's doing.
curious.body:
In There were two alarms ringing, the sentence introduces two alarms and then says what they were doing: ringing. The word ringing tells us about the alarms themselves.

A different kind of added phrase works another way. It can comment on the whole situation without describing the thing introduced. So the same sentence shape can hold either a description of the alarms or a comment on the whole event, and this dictionary keeps the two apart.

examples.text: [There was a light shining] in the window.

curious.try: In There were two alarms ringing, who or what is doing the ringing?

teacher.summary: For advanced classes: there sentences that add a location or a predicate about the introduced NP.
teacher.explain: An extended existential has dummy there, be, a pivot NP, and an integrated location or secondary predication: There were two alarms ringing. It introduces a referent and characterizes its position or current situation. Ringing predicates an activity of the alarms. A free event adjunct can instead modify the whole existential assertion without predicating a property of the pivot. This dictionary is a specialization of existential there, marked provisional, with medium confidence.
teacher.terms: Pivot NP is the NP after be. Secondary predication is a predicate that describes the pivot.

examples.text: [There was a light shining] in the window.

watch_for: A learner might treat every phrase after the pivot as describing the pivot, when a free event adjunct can modify the whole assertion.
A learner might take ringing as a separate clause, when it predicates an activity of the alarms.
teacher.activity: Students write There was/were sentences about a picture, adding what each thing is doing. Pairs then check that each added phrase describes the thing just introduced.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Extended Existential with a Predicate." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/extended-existential-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
